assumptions.original: One Euclidean Brownian motion under the sample measure μ, relative to the given filtration. The coordinates in a finite index set J come from this same motion. The sample measure is finite. The horizon T is positive and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions. For each level n and coordinate j, the stored dyadic elementary process has level n. Its bounded left-endpoint measurable coefficients have fourth moments bounded by one common real constant C over all n, cells and coordinates.
assumptions.reconstructed: B starts at zero for every omega, has jointly independent increments over disjoint half-open intervals, every continuous real linear functional ell sends B_t-B_s (s<t) to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||², and paths are continuous mu-a.e. B is strongly adapted to F and B_t-B_s is independent of F_s for s≤t. F is right-continuous and every subset S⊆Omega with mu(S)=0 belongs to F_t for every t≥0. The elementary data have strictly increasing times t_i^n=iT/2^n; each coefficient a_{n,j,i} is strongly measurable for the left-endpoint sigma-algebra F_{t_i^n} and pointwise bounded by some finite constant allowed to depend on n,j,i. For all n,j,i, ∫a_{n,j,i}^4 dmu≤C. The embedding eta_{n,j} has exactly the elementary step-process value: eta_{n,j}(t,omega)=∑_{i=0}^{2^n-1}1_{t_i^n<t≤t_{i+1}^n} a_{n,j,i}(omega), including zero at t=0 and outside (0,T].

conclusion.original: At each level of a dyadic grid, take a row of completed Itô integrals of elementary processes on that level's grid. The sum of the squared row increments minus the row's time energy is square integrable at each level and tends to zero in mean absolute value. Formula: \begin{gathered}Q_n=\sum_i(\Delta_i R_n)^2,\qquad E_n=\sum_j\int_0^T q_{n,j}(t)^2\,dt,\\ Q_n-E_n\in L^2(\mu),\qquad \int|Q_n-E_n|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0.\end{gathered}
conclusion.reconstructed: I_j(a)(t,omega) denotes the specified completed Ito integral driven by the scalar coordinate B^j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j. Its representative is the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic integrals off the null complement of their uniform Cauchy event, and zero on that complement; it is held constant after T. Put Y_n(t)=∑_{j∈J}I_j(eta_{n,j})(t) and E_n(omega)=∑_{i=0}^{2^n-1}(Y_n(t_{i+1}^n,omega)-Y_n(t_i^n,omega))²-∑_{j∈J}∫eta_{n,j}(t,omega)² d lambda_T(t). Then E_n∈L²(mu) for every n and lim_{n→infinity}∫|E_n| dmu=0.
